content.title: About
content.content: Italian sausage is a traditional pork sausage seasoned with fennel, garlic, paprika and other spices. It is widely used in Italian cuisine, especially in tomato‑based sauces, pasta dishes and pizza.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: There are two main varieties: sweet (with sweet fennel) and hot (with added red pepper).
Traditionally the sausage is made from a blend of pork and beef, though some regions use only pork.
Fennel, the key flavoring, gives the sausage its distinctive anise‑like aroma.
Italian sausage is a staple in dishes like cavatelli with sausage and tomato sauce.
In the United States it is often sold as fresh ground sausage that must be cooked before eating.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Pork provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: The sausage supplies heme iron, which is readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains B12, B6 and niacin, supporting nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Beneficial fats
items.content: A modest amount of monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats can support heart health when consumed in moderation.

items.title: Antioxidants from spices
items.content: Fennel, garlic and paprika provide antioxidant compounds that may protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Sausage is often salty; excess sodium can raise blood pressure.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Saturated fat content may contribute to elevated cholesterol if eaten frequently.

items.title: Allergy to spices
items.content: Some individuals may react to fennel, garlic or other seasonings.

items.title: Risk of foodborne illness
items.content: Raw or undercooked sausage can harbor pathogenic bacteria; it should be cooked to an internal temperature of at least 71 °C.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sausage can be pan‑fried, baked, simmered in sauces, added to pasta, pizza, stews or used as a filling for stuffed vegetables and sandwiches. For a lighter dish, trim excess fat before cooking.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh sausage refrigerated at 0–4 °C for 2–3 days. Frozen sausage can be stored up to 2 months at –18 °C. Before use, check for off‑odors or discoloration; discard if any signs of spoilage are present.
